scope: Reclaim superseded resident values at complete durable frame boundaries, identically during live publication and private replay. Latest rows and tombstones remain; affected old snapshots fail. Receipts, conflict validation, upload allowances and durable collection cuts are unchanged.

workload.context: Three stock Kubernetes hosts; B2; native release image localhost:32000/durable-db@sha256:2831974c96e1ca08797559e0e69ac000657903658b1163c02e30fc179055476c; see resources.json for limits and counters.
limitations: Small samples are descriptive, not an SLO guarantee.
Closed-loop load does not measure queue growth at a fixed arrival rate.
Provider request counts, billed storage, and cost are not measured.
Setup is excluded; retries, backoff, and failed operations are included in each measured phase.

high_concurrency_slow_work.limitations: Slow-operation logs omit fast calls. Timers overlap and are not summed client-time attribution. Counts are not all provider requests.

high_concurrency_read_slow_work.limitations: Events are assigned by completion timestamp; work may start in the preceding phase. Timers overlap and do not establish complete causal attribution.

focused_regression.negative_control: Removing only live reclamation fails at overwrite 40 (zero-based), the 41st write. Candidate restored immediately.
focused_regression.replay_negative_control: Removing only replay reclamation fails cold recovery with native recovery capacity exhausted; candidate restored immediately.

verification.real_http: 100 sequential 64 KiB overwrites, point/ordered read and exact revision over TCP with checkpoint uploads disabled; zero checkpoint attempts.
verification.adversarial: Expired value snapshots refuse; unchanged database snapshots remain valid; stale conflict validation and exact retries survive reclamation. Latest tombstones mask base values, empty values survive, both scan directions agree.

tla.limits: Two keys, three commits, three resident versions, deletion/empty/nonempty values, four query revisions, one-live-key/two-byte logical quota. Reclamation keeps the latest row per key and advances a read floor. Component check, not Rust refinement or complete protocol proof.

removed: Resident snapshot floor moved into Memory; duplicate floor field and initialization removed.
Obsolete all-history model counting helper removed.
Runtime negative-control mutation restored immediately; no parallel implementation retained.
limitations: Longer overwrite suffixes depend on reclamation during recovery; homogeneous deployment is required. Mixed-version rolling upgrades and rollback remain outside the 1.0 guarantee.
Reclamation is a bounded linear scan under exclusive projection access; configured payload allowances are not a whole-process RSS ceiling.

Unique live values, receipts, conflict history and journal frame bounds still require checkpoints; reclamation never permits journal collection. Fewer checkpoints can retain more journal objects until those bounds are reached; this run is not a cloud cold-recovery or billing qualification.
Closed-loop short run; random database placement and provider conditions differ from previous releases.
Prepared journal counters include setup/catalog work and failed uploads, not successful PUTs or provider billing.
No sustained-load, open-loop arrival-rate, p99, or availability SLO qualification.
Existing single-trust-domain 1.0 support scope is unchanged.
